product.name: Throughline
product.description: A product-discovery workspace for Business Analysts and Product Managers: build personas, journey maps, hypotheses and roadmaps with backlogs, with every claim linked to interview evidence. It sits between research (transcripts, clips) and delivery (Jira, Linear), turning tagged quotes into living personas, journeys and prioritized bets that keep their source links.

personas.name: Traceability-Driven Business Analyst
personas.tagline: The analyst who has to prove where every requirement came from
personas.description: Across a digital agency, an enterprise insurer and a lean fintech, the BA turns interviews into personas, journeys, assumptions and backlog items and is accountable for correctness, not outcome. The sharpest pain is that quotes detach from their source: Daria hunts for which interview said a line, Henrik loses three hours a week to broken Jira links, and Oksana spends an hour each time someone asks where a backlog item came from. They want an AI first draft they can see the receipts for and a one-click link into Jira or Linear, but they split on how heavy the traceability should be and whether a synthesized persona can be signed.
goals: Make the client or business confident they are building the right thing
Keep every claim linked to a confirmable source, from interview to requirement to ticket
Turn a pile of interviews into personas and journeys faster than a blank Miro board
Stop re-typing the same insight across Miro, Notion, Jira and Linear
Produce artifacts that survive sign-off, audit and handoff
frustrations: Quotes become un-sourced text the moment they land on a slide
Links break whenever a ticket is renamed, and the matrix is maintained by hand
Personas are a deliverable nobody is paid to keep alive
Prioritization scoring turns into theater rather than calculation
A new tool means another island, or a nine-month procurement cycle
personas.evidence_note: Three BA interviews with heavy does/pays evidence, plus two cross-tagged quotes from the PM interviews (260925-marcus-12, 261002-priya-11) where PMs describe the BA's sourcing discipline. Within the persona there is real disagreement on traceability depth: Henrik wants a full chain while Oksana explicitly rejects corporate ID matrices (260918-oksana-23). Accessibility/WCAG and non-interview evidence are thin: only Henrik raises them (260911-henrik-10, -11, -25).

jobs.statement: When I drop in an interview, I want a highlighted line to become a linked persona quote, journey pain and backlog source, so I can defend any requirement later.
When a stakeholder asks where a claim came from, I want to click to the exact clip in seconds, so I am not hunting across three tools.
When I synthesize a persona, I want an AI first draft I can see the receipts for and edit, so I never start from a blank board.
When I move a pain into the backlog, I want a one-click linked ticket in Jira or Linear, so the reasoning survives the handoff.
When I produce an artifact, I want it structured, accessible and version-controlled, so it passes audit and sign-off.
When evidence is not an interview, I want to link a regulation or data point as a source too, so the chain is complete.
When I share with a client or hand off to devs, I want mobile-readable views and a public link, so the artifact does not go stale as a PDF.
When I bring a new tool in, I want it priced under my incumbent anchor and able to pass SSO and procurement, so I can actually adopt it.

personas.name: Decision-Driven Product Manager
personas.tagline: The PM who judges every artifact by whether it changes a decision
personas.description: At a B2B SaaS and a marketplace, the PM runs their own discovery, owns the roadmap fully and lives in Linear, Amplitude and call recordings. They want AI to transcribe, tag and surface clips, and would pay for that, but they refuse AI-synthesized personas because the sensemaking is the work. They disagree sharply among themselves: Marcus calls personas dead artifacts updated zero times in eighteen months, while Priya refreshes hers quarterly and insists the argument, not the document, is the output. Their recurring job is to make the roadmap defensible in a 45-minute exec review, opening with a customer clip rather than a slide of themes.
goals: Make the roadmap defensible in the exec room, fast
Stop building something nobody asked for
Surface the right customer clips without scrubbing recordings
Keep the link from a clip to the Linear ticket alive
Get the whole squad to see what the PM saw
frustrations: Personas and journey maps go stale and become authoritative-looking but dead
Dovetail clips link to the whole project, not the moment, and do not survive
Rebuilding a demand spreadsheet by hand every quarter before the exec review
A new tool is a new silo, login and license to justify to finance
Juniors treating an AI persona as the answer
personas.evidence_note: Two PM interviews with heavy does/pays evidence, plus three cross-tagged quotes from Oksana, the BA/half-PM, who expresses product-manager jobs (260918-oksana-06, -10, -12). There is genuine intra-persona disagreement: Marcus treats personas as dead artifacts (260925-marcus-04, -09) while Priya maintains and values them (261002-priya-07, -08). Exec-roadmap communication rests only on the two PMs; the AI-synthesis refusal is strong across both, and is directly contradicted by the BA Oksana who is pro-synthesis (260918-oksana-15).

jobs.statement: When I prep for a decision, I want the right customer clips surfaced automatically, so I stop scrubbing recordings.
When I move an insight to delivery, I want a Linear ticket linked to the exact clip, so the why survives three weeks later.
When I face execs, I want a one-pager of bets, the one metric and the demand behind each, so the roadmap is defensible in 45 minutes.
When research lands, I want the squad to see what I saw through a two-minute clip, so engineers build the right thing.
When I frame a bet, I want the problem, bet and metric with two or three quotes on the roadmap item, not in a separate tool.
When I consider an artifact, I want it to change a decision or not exist, so nothing stale but authoritative survives.
When I adopt a tool, it must replace something and cost under my team cap, so finance does not kill it in January.
When I own the roadmap, I want BAs in the discovery but not deciding what to build, so strategy stays PM work.

business_analyst.title: Scope & plan research
business_analyst.goal: Decide what to learn and line up the interviews across competing projects

pains.text: The sole BA is stretched across four concurrent projects, one too many.
Research time is squeezed: only 8-10 interviews a quarter when 20 are wanted.

jobs.text: Juggle requirements, roadmap input and client conversations with a tiny team.

tools.text: Notion and Google Sheets to track who to talk to and what to ask.

our_flow.text: Throughline would hold a research plan tying questions to the assumptions they test.

business_analyst.title: Interview & gather evidence
business_analyst.goal: Capture interviews so that any line can later be reused and sourced

pains.text: Ten to twelve hours a week are lost moving notes across Miro, Notion, Linear, Sheets and Amplitude.
Ukrainian interviews must be translated by hand before anything reaches English tickets.

jobs.text: Make a highlighted line reusable as a persona quote, a journey pain and a backlog source at once.

tools.text: Zoom to record, Notion for one page per interview.

our_flow.text: Today there is no single place that transcribes, translates and keeps every clip addressable.

features.text: Highlight-to-artifact capture that keeps the source link on every reuse.
Bilingual transcript handling that keeps the original Ukrainian and translates.

business_analyst.title: Synthesize personas
business_analyst.goal: Turn clustered evidence into a persona the team will trust

pains.text: Clustering six interviews by hand is a full day, and building the persona takes up to six working days.
Once a quote is on a slide, the BA cannot find which interview it came from, and has misattributed one in the room.

jobs.text: Get a grounded first-draft persona to edit rather than staring at a blank board.

tools.text: Miro or FigJam stickies to cluster, Google Slides or Notion for the one-pager; Dovetail trialed but an island.

our_flow.text: An AI draft is welcome only with per-statement receipts; Henrik would still not sign a synthesized persona.

features.text: AI tagging and theme clustering that proposes a draft persona with confirmable source links.

business_analyst.title: Map customer journeys
business_analyst.goal: Produce a journey map that is both workshop-friendly and audit-ready

pains.text: The map hangs in Miro while tasks live in Jira or Linear, and within a month they drift apart.
A Miro export is an image, not a controlled document, and a blind colleague literally cannot read it.

jobs.text: Keep a structured, WCAG-compliant text version of every journey alongside the visual.

tools.text: Miro or FigJam for the workshop, then redraw into Visio or a Confluence table.

our_flow.text: No tool today gives them structured-first, accessible, versioned maps without losing the collaborative whiteboard.

features.text: Structured, accessible, version-controlled artifacts with an approval trail and controlled export.

business_analyst.title: Frame & trace assumptions
business_analyst.goal: Record assumptions and tie each to the evidence that tests it

pains.text: Assumptions live in scattered Notion or Excel registers, often only half the projects or half the rows kept live.
Hypotheses link to a Notion page, not the exact moment, and metrics are pulled from Amplitude by hand.

jobs.text: Link a hypothesis to its interview quote, its metric and its ticket in one place.

tools.text: Notion and Excel assumption registers, around forty rows per initiative.

our_flow.text: Non-interview evidence, regulations and data, should be linkable as first-class sources, which no current tool does.

features.text: Hypothesis objects that link quote, metric and ticket together.
Multi-source evidence so regulations, usage data and complaints are first-class sources.

business_analyst.title: Specify requirements & backlog
business_analyst.goal: Write requirements and backlog items that stay tied to their source

pains.text: A pain point is retyped from Miro into a Jira epic and then nobody in Jira knows where it came from.
RICE and value/effort scoring become theater, abandoned when management commits a promised feature.

jobs.text: Create a linked Jira or Linear ticket from a pain or hypothesis without touching the delivery tool itself.

tools.text: Jira, Linear and Google Sheets for backlog, a two-by-two in Miro for prioritization.

our_flow.text: They will not replace Linear or Jira, so Throughline must be the research layer that pushes into it.

features.text: Two-way Jira/Linear sync: one click to a linked ticket, status syncs back.

business_analyst.title: Review, sign-off & trace
business_analyst.goal: Get the artifact approved and prove every requirement is grounded

pains.text: A renamed Jira ticket breaks the link; Henrik loses three hours a week fixing a hand-built matrix.
Someone asks where a backlog item came from and an hour disappears hunting across tools.
Three stakeholders return comments in three formats: Word, a PDF and an email.

jobs.text: Keep the chain interview-to-assumption-to-requirement-to-story intact so every claim links to a source.

tools.text: Excel traceability matrix and Confluence version history and approval workflow.

our_flow.text: How heavy traceability should be is contested: Henrik wants a full chain, Oksana wants only click-to-clip, and the PMs call matrices overkill.

features.text: One-click trace report that keeps links from breaking and produces the audit pack.

business_analyst.title: Maintain artifacts & hand off
business_analyst.goal: Keep artifacts alive, share them, and clear procurement

pains.text: Personas are a deliverable nobody is paid to maintain, and go stale, un-updated for a year.
At handoff the BA reconstructs a requirement's reasoning from about three tools.
A new system means a nine-month procurement cycle and nothing is considered without SSO.

jobs.text: Share a living persona or journey without making the client create an account.

tools.text: Exported PDFs and Miro boards, versus incumbent anchors Miro, Productboard and a retired requirements tool.

our_flow.text: Pricing must sit under the incumbent anchor, with agency/startup expensing under $25-35 and enterprise needing SSO on the cloud tenant.

features.text: Mobile-readable, public-link client sharing without forced accounts.

product_manager.title: Plan continuous discovery
product_manager.goal: Keep a steady cadence of customer conversations feeding the roadmap

pains.text: Volume is high: 25-30 interviews a quarter personally, 60-70 across the team, hard to manage.

jobs.text: Hold the discipline of weekly interviews, since the habit matters more than the tool.

tools.text: Zoom plus in-app recruiting prompts; Gong captures sales calls as a second stream.

our_flow.text: Throughline would track interview cadence and link each session to the bets it informs.

product_manager.title: Talk to customers
product_manager.goal: Hear customers directly and keep a live line to them

pains.text: Listening to Gong recordings at 1.5x on the train is the only way to keep up.

jobs.text: Keep a real, responsive line to customers rather than relying on archetypes.

tools.text: A Slack channel of customer champions who reply in forty minutes is Marcus's real persona.

our_flow.text: No tool today turns these live conversations into reusable, linkable clips automatically.

product_manager.title: Synthesize insights & personas
product_manager.goal: Turn calls into themes and clips the team will act on, without a dead persona

pains.text: Five tools (Zoom, Dovetail, Notion, Miro, Linear) and ~9 hours a week in Dovetail and Notion.
The link from an insight into Linear points to the whole Dovetail project, not the clip, and does not survive.

jobs.text: Surface where many calls mention the same thing, with links, without reading each by hand.

tools.text: Dovetail for tags and highlight reels, a Notion opportunities board; built by hand from ~40 interviews.

our_flow.text: Tagging and clip-finding are wanted and paid for, but auto-persona synthesis is refused: the sensemaking is the work.

features.text: AI clip-finder that surfaces N-of-M call themes with one-click clips.
Consolidate Dovetail and the Notion board into one workspace that pushes to Linear.
Optional, clearly-labeled draft synthesis a PM can shred, off by default so juniors do not paste it as truth.

product_manager.title: Map journeys & funnels
product_manager.goal: Understand the flow in a way that drives action, not a poster

pains.text: A printed journey poster sits on a wall unlooked-at; a map of emotions and smiley faces is not actionable.

jobs.text: See where users actually drop in the funnel, tied to backend events.

tools.text: Amplitude funnels for the real journey; Miro for a living map Priya updates every other month.

our_flow.text: Whether a journey map earns its keep splits the PMs: Marcus can't act on one, Priya keeps hers live and would not give up Miro.

product_manager.title: Frame bets & hypotheses
product_manager.goal: State the problem, the bet and the metric next to the work

pains.text: A separate hypothesis tool is unwanted; the bet should sit on the roadmap item itself.

jobs.text: Attach problem, bet and metric with two or three representative quotes and a call link.

tools.text: Linear ticket header carries the three lines; a standing rule requires a clip in sprint planning.

our_flow.text: Evidence depth is deliberately light: two or three quotes is enough, and the metric, not a footnote, settles a wrong bet.

features.text: Lean hypothesis-in-the-ticket with problem/bet/metric and 2-3 attached clips.

product_manager.title: Prioritize & build roadmap
product_manager.goal: Order the work and keep the reasoning attached

pains.text: The official roadmap tool (Aha!) is not where the real work lives; the working roadmap is a Linear view.
A new tool is a new silo, login and license to justify to finance, so it must sit inside Linear.

jobs.text: Keep the clip-to-ticket link alive from research into Linear.

tools.text: Linear for the working roadmap and backlog; Aha! as the company standard.

our_flow.text: Ownership is contested: the PMs own roadmap as strategy, while the BA/half-PM argues whoever researches should own it.

features.text: Clip-to-ticket Linear integration where the link resolves to the exact moment and status syncs.

product_manager.title: Communicate to execs
product_manager.goal: Win the quarterly roadmap review and answer why-this-not-that

pains.text: A 45-minute quarterly review where CFO and sales want dates is Marcus's main stress.
He rebuilds a demand spreadsheet (who asked, revenue at stake) every quarter, ~6 hours; Priya scrubs clips ~2 hours monthly.

jobs.text: Open with a customer clip and show the one number that says a bet is working.

tools.text: A now/next/later slide with confidence bands, and a hand-built demand spreadsheet.

our_flow.text: What execs want is demand and story, not archetypes; opening with a voice beats a slide of themes.

features.text: Exec one-pager: bets, the one metric and the demand (who asked, revenue) auto-assembled.
Shareable two-minute clips so an engineer can drop in and feel the customer.

pains.text: Personas updated zero times in eighteen months were, to Marcus, never load-bearing.
A stale tool is worse than no tool because people still trust it.

jobs.text: Refresh segments each quarter from new cohorts so a new segment can surface.

tools.text: Manual quarterly refresh in Miro and Notion, or no refresh at all.

our_flow.text: Whether maintained artifacts are worth it is the core PM split: Priya refreshes and finds segments, Marcus and the BA see onboarding-only or dead.

features.text: Live, auto-refreshing insights that surface only when they change a decision.

opportunities.title: Keep every claim linked to its source without maintaining a matrix by hand
Turn a pile of interviews into a first-draft persona and journey fast, with receipts
Stop re-typing insights between research and the delivery tool
Make artifacts audit-ready: accessible, versioned and approvable
Survive handoff and procurement: sharing, SSO and price
Treat non-interview evidence as a first-class source
Find the right clips and themes without scrubbing recordings
Keep a clip's link alive from research into Linear
Make the roadmap defensible in the exec room, fast
Decide whether personas and journeys are worth maintaining at all
Don't add a sixth silo: consolidate or integrate
Settle who owns the roadmap and keep BAs in discovery

solutions.title: Evidence-linked highlight-to-artifact
solutions.description: Highlight a transcript line and reuse it as a persona quote, a journey pain and a backlog source while the link travels with it. Any artifact element can be clicked back to the exact clip, so requirements stay grounded.
solutions.rationale: Named by every BA as the core job, with does/pays evidence, but build reaches across capture, personas, journeys and backlog.

solutions.title: One-click trace report & link repair
solutions.description: Keep the interview-to-requirement-to-ticket chain intact when tickets are renamed, and generate the audit trace pack in one click. It targets the enterprise evidence-gathering burden rather than everyday use.
solutions.rationale: High value but thin: Henrik alone carries the pays evidence, and two PMs plus Oksana call deep traceability overkill.

solutions.title: AI tagging & draft synthesis with confirmable sources
solutions.description: Auto-transcribe, tag quotes, cluster themes and propose a draft persona and journey where every statement links to the source quote the BA confirms. The draft is editable, never an unsourced black box.
solutions.rationale: Strong demand for tagging plus a sourced draft, but synthesis trust is contested, so confidence rests on the confirm-each-tag design.

solutions.title: Two-way Jira/Linear sync
solutions.description: One click turns a pain or hypothesis into a Jira or Linear ticket with a backlink to the quote, and status changes sync back. Throughline stays the research layer; it never replaces the delivery tool.
solutions.rationale: Integration is named mandatory and gates willingness to pay; does evidence across two BAs.

solutions.title: Structured, accessible, versioned artifacts
solutions.description: Every persona and journey has a WCAG-compliant structured text representation with version history, an approval workflow and an audit trail, and exports as a controlled document, not just an image.
solutions.rationale: A hard enterprise requirement but thin: only Henrik raises accessibility and controlled-document needs.

solutions.title: Multi-source evidence beyond interviews
solutions.description: Link regulations, usage data, support tickets and complaints as first-class sources alongside interview quotes, so the assumption and requirement chain is complete for non-interview evidence.
solutions.rationale: Clearly useful but thin: raised by Henrik alone, so impact and confidence are held low.

solutions.title: Low-friction bilingual capture
solutions.description: A draft in minutes with minimal required fields, and transcript handling that ingests Ukrainian interviews, keeps the original and translates quotes into the English used for tickets and docs.
solutions.rationale: Bilingual handling is a hard blocker for Oksana, but evidence is single-interviewee and said-level.

solutions.title: Client-ready mobile & public-link sharing
solutions.description: Read-only persona and journey views that are readable on a phone and shareable through a public link without forcing the client to create an account, so the shared artifact never goes stale as an exported PDF.
solutions.rationale: A clear agency need but thin: Daria alone, said-level, so scored as a low-effort delighter.

solutions.title: AI clip-finder & theme surfacing
solutions.description: Transcribe calls, tag them and surface patterns like fourteen of thirty calls mention re-sequencing, with one-click clips, and pull the three best clips for any roadmap item from a single place. It kills the hours of scrubbing before a review.
solutions.rationale: Both PMs explicitly want it and say they would pay, so pays evidence from two people supports full confidence.

solutions.title: Clip-to-ticket Linear integration
solutions.description: One click turns an insight into a Linear ticket whose link resolves to the exact clip, not the whole project, and status syncs back. Throughline sits on top of Linear so the PM never has to visit a separate destination.
solutions.rationale: Integration is the named precondition for adoption and for paying more; does evidence from both PMs.

solutions.title: Exec-ready roadmap one-pager with demand
solutions.description: Assemble a now/next/later one-pager with confidence bands, the one metric per bet, and the demand behind each item (which customers asked, revenue at stake), so the PM stops rebuilding a spreadsheet every quarter and can answer why-this-not-that in seconds.
solutions.rationale: Clear does evidence but confined to the two PMs; the exec-communication job does not appear in the BA interviews.

solutions.title: Opt-in draft synthesis a PM can shred
solutions.description: A clearly-labeled, editable draft persona built only from confirmable sources, off by default, with guardrails so a junior cannot paste it into a deck as the answer. It is deliberately minimal because PMs will not pay for synthesis.
solutions.rationale: Scored low on purpose: both PMs refuse AI synthesis, and the only pull is cross-persona from the BA Oksana.

solutions.title: Shareable clips for the whole squad
solutions.description: Make it trivial for an engineer to drop in, watch a two-minute clip and feel the customer, so research spreads and the team shares the understanding rather than one PM carrying it.
solutions.rationale: A compelling job but thin: carried mainly by Priya at said-level.

solutions.title: Live, decision-gated insights
solutions.description: Personas and journeys that refresh from new cohorts and only surface when they would change a decision, avoiding the stale-but-authoritative trap. It explicitly serves the PMs who maintain artifacts and sidesteps those who find them dead.
solutions.rationale: Directly contested: Priya maintains and values refresh while Marcus and the BA call personas dead or onboarding-only, so confidence stays low.

solutions.title: Lean hypothesis-in-the-ticket
solutions.description: Attach the problem, the bet and the metric to the roadmap item with two or three representative quotes and the call link, so the PM never opens a separate hypothesis tool.
solutions.rationale: Low effort and welcomed, but it mostly formalizes what Marcus already does by hand, so impact is modest.

solutions.title: One-workspace consolidation (replace, don't add)
solutions.description: Replace Dovetail and the Notion opportunity board with a single workspace doing clips, tags, the opportunity tree and push-to-Linear. It must replace tools, not become a sixth silo, or a PM like Marcus will refuse it outright.
solutions.rationale: Priya would happily consolidate and pay more, but Marcus's stack-works stance keeps this from being a universal must.

sources.summary: Daria is the sole BA across four projects at a 60-person digital agency, spending ~12 hours a week arranging artifacts in Miro, Slides and Notion. Her sharpest pains are quotes detaching from their source, retyping between tools, and reconstructing reasoning at handoff; she wants one linked place and an AI first-draft she can see the receipts for.

Henrik is a senior BA in enterprise insurance claims where every requirement needs a source, an owner and a sign-off, and personas are a funded, audited control point. He maintains a hand-built traceability matrix in Excel, loses three hours a week to broken links, accepts AI tagging only with confirmation but refuses AI-synthesized personas, and is gated by a nine-month procurement cycle and mandatory SSO. He is the only interviewee raising accessibility and non-interview evidence.

Oksana is a formally-BA, half-PM at a fast-growing fintech where she writes requirements, runs the roadmap and talks to clients with a two-and-a-half-person product team. Her interviews are in Ukrainian while tickets are in English, so bilingual transcript handling is a hard requirement. She wants auto-synthesis with source links, mandatory Linear integration, a low-friction draft-in-minutes flow, and light click-to-clip traceability rather than corporate matrices, with price anchored under Productboard.

Marcus is a senior PM at a B2B construction-SaaS firm who calls personas and journey maps dead artifacts and judges everything by whether it changes a decision. He runs lean: hypotheses live in the Linear ticket, two or three quotes are enough evidence, and his real work is making the roadmap defensible in a 45-minute exec review. He wants AI theme-and-quote surfacing but would never open an auto-persona, and anything new must live inside Linear, not become a sixth silo.

Priya runs continuous discovery on the seller side of a marketplace, doing 25-30 interviews a quarter and refreshing hand-built behavioral personas every quarter. She lives across five tools, and her sharpest gap is that Dovetail clips do not survive the link into Linear. She wants AI tagging and one-click clip-pulling and would pay well for it, but refuses AI synthesis because the sensemaking is the work and she fears junior PMs treating an AI persona as the answer.

nuggets.text: She would worry about a generated persona only if it had no grounding she could click through.
nuggets.quote: I'd worry if it had no grounding.

nuggets.text: Every requirement needs a source, an owner and a sign-off because auditors ask.
nuggets.quote: Every requirement needs a source, an owner, a sign-off.

nuggets.text: He spends about twenty hours a week in Confluence, Word and Excel and ten more in Jira.
nuggets.quote: I would spend, honestly, twenty hours a week in Confluence and Word and Excel, and another ten in Jira.

nuggets.text: He never creates personas from nothing; he extends the six approved ones because the design authority must approve them.
nuggets.quote: When I start an initiative I take the relevant persona and extend it. I do not create from nothing, because everything must be approved by the design authority.

nuggets.text: Updating the broker persona from nine interviews took three weeks, almost all of it review rounds.
nuggets.quote: I did the broker one myself, from nine interviews, and it took me three weeks, because of the review rounds.

nuggets.text: Three stakeholders return comments in three different formats: Word tracked changes, a PDF with sticky notes, and an email.
nuggets.quote: Three stakeholders, each with comments in a different format. One in Word with tracked changes, one in a PDF with sticky notes, one in an email.

nuggets.text: A project cannot pass the funding gate without naming its persona and linking the journey.
nuggets.quote: A new project cannot get funding gate approval without naming the persona it serves and linking the journey.

nuggets.text: Personas are a control point and a shared language across business, IT and compliance.
nuggets.quote: A control point and a shared language. Between business, IT, compliance.

nuggets.text: Compliance limits Miro to workshops, so he redraws every journey into Visio or a Confluence table.
nuggets.quote: Miro is for workshops only and then I redraw into Visio or into Confluence with a table.

nuggets.text: A Miro export is an image, and an image is not accepted as a controlled document.
nuggets.quote: the export from Miro is an image, and an image is not accepted as a controlled document.

nuggets.text: Internal documents must meet WCAG because some staff use screen readers.
nuggets.quote: We are required to meet WCAG standards for internal documents too, since some of our staff use screen readers.

nuggets.text: A blind claims-handler colleague literally cannot read the team's Miro exports.
nuggets.quote: I have a colleague who is blind, she is a claims handler, and she literally cannot read our Miro exports.

nuggets.text: He keeps an assumptions register of around forty rows per initiative in Excel.
nuggets.quote: I keep a register in Excel, around forty rows per initiative.

nuggets.text: His traceability chain runs from interview evidence to assumption to requirement to story to test case.
nuggets.quote: Interview evidence, to assumption, to requirement, to story, to test case.

nuggets.text: His rule is that every claim must link to a source, or it is just an opinion.
nuggets.quote: Every claim must link to a source, otherwise it is an opinion.

nuggets.text: When someone renames a Jira ticket his link dies, and he spends about three hours a week fixing links.
nuggets.quote: Someone renames a Jira ticket and my link is dead. I spend maybe three hours a week fixing links.

nuggets.text: He holds that the roadmap belongs to the product owner, while he owns the backlog's quality.
nuggets.quote: The roadmap belongs to the product owner and the head of product. Not to me. I own the backlog's quality

nuggets.text: He argues the BA should not own roadmap: the product owner is accountable for outcome, the BA for correctness.
nuggets.quote: The product owner is accountable for outcome. I am accountable for correctness.

nuggets.text: A persona is a statement the insurer is willing to be audited on, so an AI-produced one makes him nervous.
nuggets.quote: a persona is a statement that the bank, sorry, the insurer, is willing to be audited on.

nuggets.text: He could accept AI tagging as a first pass as long as he confirms each tag.
nuggets.quote: I could accept that for tagging, as a first pass, as long as I confirm each tag.

nuggets.text: He would not sign a synthesized persona he did not construct himself.
nuggets.quote: A synthesized persona that I did not construct, I would not sign.

nuggets.text: A new system means procurement and security review, which runs roughly nine months at his company.
nuggets.quote: It would be another system to bring through procurement and security review. In this company that is, roughly, nine months.

nuggets.text: If a tool produced the audit trace report in one click, his director would push for it.
nuggets.quote: If a tool produced the trace report in one click, she would listen.

nuggets.text: A department might accept forty to sixty euros per seat per month for ten seats, on their cloud tenant with SSO.
nuggets.quote: a department would perhaps accept forty to sixty euros per seat per month, for ten seats, if on our cloud tenant with SSO.

nuggets.text: He would consider nothing without SSO.
nuggets.quote: Nothing without SSO.

nuggets.text: Interviews, regulations, claims data and complaints are all sources and each should be linkable.
nuggets.quote: Interviews, regulations, claims data, complaints. All sources. Each should be linkable.

nuggets.text: He trusts Confluence's version history, approval workflow and audit trail.
nuggets.quote: Version history, approval workflow in Confluence, the audit trail.

nuggets.text: With a two-and-a-half-person product team she has to write requirements, run the roadmap and talk to clients at once.
nuggets.quote: So I have to write requirements, run the roadmap and talk to clients all at once.

nuggets.text: She spends ten to twelve hours a week across Miro, Notion, Linear, Google Sheets and Amplitude.
nuggets.quote: About ten to twelve hours a week across different tools: Miro, Notion, Linear, some Google Sheets and Amplitude.

nuggets.text: She runs only eight to ten interviews a quarter and wishes she could do twenty, but lacks hands.
nuggets.quote: I do about eight to ten interviews a quarter now. I would like twenty, but there are not enough hands.

nuggets.text: The team built their three personas once last summer, and it took about six working days.
nuggets.quote: We built them once, last summer. It took about six working days. Six days!

nuggets.text: The personas have not been updated once since, and are now stale after the team launched credit products.
nuggets.quote: Have we updated them since? No. Not once. They are probably a bit stale now, because we launched credits.

nuggets.text: The personas are mostly for onboarding new people; the team does not open them for daily decisions.
nuggets.quote: They are mostly needed for onboarding new people. For daily decisions we do not open them.

nuggets.text: Her onboarding CJM hangs in Miro while tasks live in Linear, so after a month the map and backlog drift apart.
nuggets.quote: The map hangs in Miro while the tasks live in Linear, and after a month the map and the backlog drift apart, and no one remembers which ticket came from which pain.

nuggets.text: She keeps a Notion hypotheses database of about forty entries, maybe fifteen live, with metrics pulled from Amplitude by hand.
nuggets.quote: In Notion there is a 'Hypotheses' database, about forty entries, maybe fifteen of them live, and I pull the metrics from Amplitude by hand.

nuggets.text: She wants a hypothesis linked to the interview quote, the metric and the ticket instead of three separate places.
nuggets.quote: I would like a hypothesis to be linked to the interview quote, the metric and the ticket. Right now those are three different places.

nuggets.text: Although formally a BA, she really owns the roadmap alongside the other product manager.
nuggets.quote: I run the roadmap, together with the other product manager, but really it is mine.

nuggets.text: They tried RICE in Google Sheets, but it went in the bin when management committed a feature for a promised client.
nuggets.quote: We tried RICE, and then someone in management said we do this feature because a client was promised it, and RICE went in the bin.

nuggets.text: She argues whoever does the research should own the roadmap, so the BA/PM boundary is artificial.
nuggets.quote: Whoever does the research should own the roadmap, otherwise they drift apart; I think that boundary is basically artificial.

nuggets.text: She wants to drop an interview recording in, get a transcript, highlight quotes and have it suggest tags and themes.
nuggets.quote: I want to drop in an interview recording, get a transcript, highlight quotes, and have it suggest tags and themes itself.

nuggets.text: From the themes she wants it to propose a draft persona and a draft journey map.
nuggets.quote: Then from the themes it would propose a draft persona and a draft journey map.

nuggets.text: She would happily give the model the first draft and do the second iteration herself, because fast beats perfect.
nuggets.quote: I would give the model the first draft and do the second iteration myself.

nuggets.text: Because she fears invention, every phrase must link to its source; no link means it is a fabrication.
nuggets.quote: That is exactly why every phrase must link to a source. If there is no link, it is a fabrication.

nuggets.text: She thinks big-company BAs who refuse AI-built personas are just protecting their own work.
nuggets.quote: I have heard colleagues at big companies would not accept this; I think it is just a way to protect their own work.

nuggets.text: She does not want to replace Linear, which developers love; she wants the research layer between it and discovery.
nuggets.quote: I do not need a replacement for Linear; Linear is good, developers love it, I will not touch it.

nuggets.text: She wants one click to create a Linear ticket from a hypothesis or pain, with a link back to the quote.
nuggets.quote: I would like one click to create a Linear ticket from a hypothesis or pain, with a link back to the quote.

nuggets.text: Without Linear integration she would not pay, since it would just be another page to write in.
nuggets.quote: Mandatory. Without it, why bother? I would not pay.

nuggets.text: Productboard cost about twenty dollars per maker and only did roadmap, so Throughline must not cost more than Productboard.
nuggets.quote: We looked at Productboard but it cost about twenty dollars per maker, and your product must not cost more than Productboard.

nuggets.text: For a team of three she would pay eight to twelve dollars per seat without question, up to twenty with Linear integration and auto-synthesis.
nuggets.quote: For a team of three I would say eight to twelve dollars per seat per month without question, up to twenty I can fight for if there is Linear integration and auto-synthesis.

nuggets.text: She does not want corporate traceability with ID tables; she just needs to click and see the clip.
nuggets.quote: I would not call it traceability like in big companies, not tables with IDs. I just need to click and see the clip. We are not auditors.

nuggets.text: When someone asks where a backlog item came from, she spends at least an hour hunting, two or three times a month.
nuggets.quote: The moment someone asks where did we get this from, I spend at least an hour on it each time.

nuggets.text: She values FigJam for being fast and convenient for team workshops.
nuggets.quote: FigJam. For team workshops it is very convenient and fast.

nuggets.text: A tool that cannot handle Ukrainian transcripts, pull quotes keeping the original and translate them is useless to her.
nuggets.quote: My interviews are in Ukrainian but tickets and docs are in English. If your tool cannot handle Ukrainian transcripts, pull quotes keeping the original, and translate, it is useless to me.

nuggets.text: Aha! is the company standard but his real working roadmap is a Linear project with a view he trusts.
nuggets.quote: my real working roadmap is a Linear project with a view I trust.

nuggets.text: He listens to Gong recordings of sales calls at one and a half speed on the train.
nuggets.quote: Gong recordings from sales calls, I listen to those at one and a half speed on the train.

nuggets.text: His real persona is a Slack channel of customer champions who reply in forty minutes.
nuggets.quote: That's my persona. A real person who replies in forty minutes.

nuggets.text: The commissioned personas are dead artifacts that went in a folder and nobody opens.
nuggets.quote: They're dead artifacts. That's my phrase.

nuggets.text: The printed onboarding journey map is a poster on a Berlin office wall that he has never seen anyone look at.
nuggets.quote: It is on a wall in the Berlin office and I've never seen anyone look at it.

nuggets.text: He looks at the real journey as an Amplitude funnel: where people drop between sign-up and first published schedule.
nuggets.quote: The actual journey I look at in Amplitude: where do people drop between sign-up and first published schedule.

nuggets.text: A journey map with emotions and little smiley faces is something he cannot act on.
nuggets.quote: A map with emotions, little smiley faces, I can't act on.

nuggets.text: He argues the artifact is not the point; the point is whether it changes a decision, else why maintain it.
nuggets.quote: The point is decisions. Does it change a decision? If not, why maintain it.

nuggets.text: Their personas have been updated zero times in eighteen months, which to him means they were not load-bearing.
nuggets.quote: Ours has been updated zero times in eighteen months. And I don't think that's a failure. It means they weren't load-bearing.

nuggets.text: Each Linear initiative has three lines at the top: the problem, the bet and the metric.
nuggets.quote: Each initiative in Linear has three lines at the top: the problem, the bet, the metric.

nuggets.text: He pastes two or three representative quotes and a call link into the Linear ticket, and considers that enough.
nuggets.quote: I paste two or three representative quotes into the Linear ticket and a link to the call. Two or three. That's enough.

nuggets.text: He has seen BAs want every claim linked to a source with IDs and a matrix, which he considers overkill.
nuggets.quote: I've heard BAs I've worked with want every claim to link to a source, with IDs and a matrix. I think that's overkill.

nuggets.text: If a decision is wrong he finds out from the metric, not from the footnote.
nuggets.quote: If a decision is wrong we find out from the metric, not from the footnote.

nuggets.text: He owns the roadmap fully; where he saw a BA own it, it turned into a requirements list, because a roadmap is a strategy argument.
nuggets.quote: I've worked at a place where the BA owned the roadmap and it turned into a requirements list. A roadmap is a strategy argument. That's PM work.

nuggets.text: Every quarter he defends the roadmap in a 45-minute review with the CEO, CFO, head of sales and head of customer success.
nuggets.quote: Every quarter there's a roadmap review with the CEO, CFO, head of sales, head of customer success. I have forty-five minutes.

nuggets.text: Instead of the dates the CFO and sales want, he gives confidence bands: committed, likely, exploring.
nuggets.quote: The CFO wants dates. Sales wants dates. I give them confidence bands instead: committed, likely, exploring.

nuggets.text: He wants a one-pager stating what they are betting on and the one number that tells them it is working.
nuggets.quote: A one-pager that says here's what we're betting on and here's the one number that tells us if it's working.

nuggets.text: To answer why-this-not-that he rebuilds a demand spreadsheet of who asked and revenue at stake every quarter, about six hours.
nuggets.quote: here are the nine customers who asked, here's the revenue at stake. I do that in a spreadsheet right now. A spreadsheet I rebuild every quarter. That's maybe six hours the week before.

nuggets.text: What feeds his prioritization is demand evidence, not archetypes.
nuggets.quote: Show me demand, not archetypes.

nuggets.text: He could use the theme-and-quote part, noting Gong already does a flavor of it.
nuggets.quote: The theme-and-quote part I could use. Gong already does a flavor of it.

nuggets.text: He would never open an auto-generated persona, would not read it, and would not pay for it.
nuggets.quote: Auto-persona? I'd never open it. The tool can make it, I just won't read it. So I wouldn't pay for it.

nuggets.text: His stack works and a new tool is a new silo: another login, another thing people forget to update, another license to justify to finance.
nuggets.quote: A new tool is a new silo. It's another login, another thing people forget to update, another license I have to justify to finance in January.

nuggets.text: For him to consider it, it would have to live inside Linear or sit on top of it; if it is a destination he will not go.
nuggets.quote: It'd have to live inside Linear, or sit on top of it so that I never go there. If it's a destination, I won't go.

nuggets.text: A stale tool is worse than no tool, because people trust it.
nuggets.quote: a stale tool is worse than no tool, because people trust it.

nuggets.text: For a team total under about a hundred a month he would adopt it without asking; over three hundred finance gets involved and he says no.
nuggets.quote: If the team total is under, I don't know, a hundred a month, I'd just do it without asking. Over three hundred, finance gets involved, and I'd say no.

nuggets.text: He wants something that changes what he does Monday morning, not a place for artifacts: artifacts are the hobby, decisions the job.
nuggets.quote: Build something that changes what I do on Monday morning. Artifacts are the hobby; decisions are the job.

nuggets.text: She follows continuous discovery, personally doing about twenty-five to thirty interviews a quarter recruited by in-app prompt.
nuggets.quote: In a quarter, between us, we do about sixty to seventy interviews. Mine personally is about twenty-five to thirty.

nuggets.text: Her team has a standing rule: no sprint planning without at least one customer clip shown.
nuggets.quote: we have a standing rule: no sprint planning without at least one customer clip shown.

nuggets.text: Her flow spans five tools: Zoom, Dovetail, Notion, Miro and Linear.
nuggets.quote: So that's Zoom, Dovetail, Notion, Miro, Linear. Five tools.

nuggets.text: She spends about nine hours a week in Dovetail and Notion combined, plus two in Miro.
nuggets.quote: I'd say I spend about nine hours a week in Dovetail and Notion combined, plus two in Miro.

nuggets.text: The link from an insight into Linear points to the whole Dovetail project, not the clip, so it does not survive.
nuggets.quote: the link is to the whole Dovetail project, not to the clip. It doesn't survive.

nuggets.text: She built her seller segments by hand from about forty interviews using printed transcripts and highlighters.
nuggets.quote: Printed transcripts, a table, highlighters, the whole nonsense.

nuggets.text: For her the persona is not the output; the argument is the output and the document is just the receipt.
nuggets.quote: The persona isn't the output. The argument is the output. The document is just the receipt.

nuggets.text: She refreshes personas lightly every quarter and bigger every six months, which surfaced a fourth estate-clearing segment.
nuggets.quote: Every quarter, a light refresh. Every six months, bigger.

nuggets.text: Her journey map per core flow carries the emotional curve and the backend events and is updated every other month.
nuggets.quote: It has the emotional curve and also the actual backend events. It's updated, I would say, every other month.

nuggets.text: She requires clips only for the load-bearing claims and top ten opportunities, not for everything.
nuggets.quote: For the load-bearing ones, yes. For the top ten opportunities, I want clips. For everything, no, that's absurd, I'd never finish.

nuggets.text: Her BA friend at a bank keeps a matrix with every claim sourced, a discipline she could not live with.
nuggets.quote: I have a BA friend at a bank who has a matrix with every claim sourced. I couldn't live like that.

nuggets.text: A thirty-second clip of a seller in their own voice is the most persuasive object in product management.
nuggets.quote: a clip, thirty seconds of a seller saying it in their own voice, is the most persuasive object in product management.

nuggets.text: Because execs want the story not the roadmap, she opens the monthly review with two minutes of clips.
nuggets.quote: the execs don't want the roadmap, they want the story. I open with two minutes of clips.

nuggets.text: She wants to pull the three best clips for a roadmap item in one click, from a single place.
nuggets.quote: Being able to pull the three best clips for a roadmap item in one click, from a single place.

nuggets.text: She scrubs recordings about twenty minutes per item for six items, roughly two hours before each monthly meeting.
nuggets.quote: Right now I scrub through recordings. Twenty minutes per item, and I'd do six items.

nuggets.text: She owns the roadmap; BAs own requirements and edge cases and she wants them in the discovery, not deciding what to build.
nuggets.quote: they own requirements and edge cases. I don't want them deciding what to build. But I want them in the discovery.

nuggets.text: For tagging and clip-finding she would pay, since surfacing moments saves her hours.
nuggets.quote: For tagging and clip-finding, yes, please, I'd pay for that.

nuggets.text: A persona she did not build herself she would not trust, so she refuses the AI synthesis.
nuggets.quote: A persona I didn't build, I wouldn't trust.

nuggets.text: The sensemaking is the work; automating it removes the part that makes her good at the job.
nuggets.quote: The sensemaking is the work. If you automate it, you automate away the part that makes me good at the job.

nuggets.text: She fears junior PMs on her team will take an AI persona as the answer rather than shredding it.
nuggets.quote: That's what I'd be afraid of for junior PMs on my team: they take the AI persona as the answer.

nuggets.text: She would replace Dovetail and the Notion database with one thing doing clips, tags, opportunity tree and push-to-Linear, but will not add a sixth tool.
nuggets.quote: I would happily replace Dovetail and the Notion database with one thing, if it could do clips, tags, opportunity tree and push to Linear.

nuggets.text: She would not give up Miro for live workshops because whiteboarding is human.
nuggets.quote: And Miro for the live workshops, I wouldn't give up. Whiteboarding is human.

nuggets.text: Against a Dovetail anchor of about thirty a seat, she would pay forty to forty-five per seat without blinking and justify fifty-five.
nuggets.quote: I'd pay forty, forty-five per seat per month, and I wouldn't blink. Fifty-five, I'd have to justify it.

nuggets.text: She would pay even more for Linear integration, because that is where her three weeks of why-did-we-do-this lives.
nuggets.quote: I'd go higher if it integrated with Linear, genuinely

nuggets.text: Her core job is to get everyone to see what she saw, because research is only valuable if the team shares the understanding.
nuggets.quote: Research is only valuable if the team shares the understanding.

nuggets.text: The tool should make it easy for an engineer to drop in, watch a two-minute clip and feel it.
nuggets.quote: The tool should make it easy for an engineer to drop in, watch a two-minute clip, and feel it.

hypotheses.name: H1 One tool over the stack
hypotheses.statement: BAs and PMs would adopt a single discovery workspace instead of stitching Miro, Notion, Jira and Linear, but only if it integrates with their existing delivery tool rather than becoming a sixth silo.

hypotheses.name: H2 Tag yes, synthesis no
hypotheses.statement: Users want AI to transcribe, tag quotes and find clips, but distrust AI-synthesized personas and journey maps unless every statement links to a confirmable source quote they can review.

hypotheses.name: H3 Traceability depth splits BA vs PM
hypotheses.statement: Deep claim-to-source traceability (IDs, matrices, every claim sourced) is a must-have for BAs but is seen as overkill by most PMs, who source only the load-bearing claims.

hypotheses.name: H4 Dead artifacts
hypotheses.statement: Personas and journey maps become dead, unmaintained artifacts after they are presented, unless maintaining them is funded or they visibly change a roadmap decision.

hypotheses.name: H5 Price & procurement gate adoption
hypotheses.statement: Enterprise adoption is gated by SSO, data residency and a nine-month procurement cycle, while agency and startup adoption is gated by a per-seat price anchored under an incumbent like Productboard or Dovetail.

hypotheses.name: H6 Evidence beyond interviews
hypotheses.statement: Users need to link non-interview evidence such as regulations, usage data, support tickets and complaints as first-class sources, not only interview quotes.
